title: Paramitas - Patience Beyond Patience (Kshanti)
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up kshanti paramita, the practice of patience on the bodhisattva's list of six, and reads the Sanskrit as "unaffected by, or able to be with" and paramita as "patience beyond patience." Nomon contrasts the Western picture of patience as putting up with an idiot and as a fixed trait with a practice of merging, where impatience becomes information and a seed that can sprout. Mary Oliver's poem "I Worried" shows how many times "I" appears in a worrying narrative. A Prajnaparamita passage about giving away even one's life to robbers meets Aristotle's idea that one should be neither irascible nor non-irascible. Nomon closes with Seisho Maylie Scott's reply to a lonely student, "Please do not ever think anything is out of place," and a reflection on the moment the hook came out.
